title: Read field 48 by tag

blocks.text: An issuer's authorization rules need two or three items from field 48 of every incoming request. The team keeps field 48 in the packager as plain text, so that a network release that adds a subelement can never stop a message from unpacking, and reads the items in code.
`src/main/java/com/example/practice/Field48Reader.java` already hands the rules what they ask for through `wanted`. Finish the two methods it relies on:

items: `categoryCode`: the transaction category code, or `null` when the field has none;
`value`: the data of the subelement with a given two-digit tag, or `null` when the field doesn't carry that tag.

blocks.text: The field arrives exactly as the network sent it. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: the category code and the data of each wanted tag are read, and a tag the field doesn't carry gives null
a tag's digits inside another subelement's data are data, so a tag is found only where a subelement starts
a field whose first character is a digit has no category code and starts with a subelement
a subelement with a tag the application doesn't use is stepped over by its length, and the ones after it are still read

origin.section: 6.4. Field 48 Is Read Tag by Tag, and an Unknown Tag Must Not Stop the Message

concepts: Field 48 is an optional category code then tag-length-value subelements, found by walking lengths, never at fixed offsets or by searching for the tag's digits.
